correctness.rationale: Off-diagonal Gram entries vanish iff first k-1 normalized Fourier moments vanish. Endpoint integration identifies differences of k endpoint power sums; Newton identities show r<k would force identical start/end endpoint multisets. For r=k, self-inversive coefficients of unit-circle-root polynomials with equal nonconstant terms and different constants imply all intermediate coefficients vanish; both endpoint sets are regular k-gons, cyclic alternation then imposes equal arcs length 2pi rho/k. Differentiated moments yield delta c_m=(sqrt(k)/(2pi))e^(-im phi)(e^(-im ell) vhat_m-uhat_m). Conjugate real Fourier blocks and even-k Nyquist case give exactly the two squared singular levels with k-1 multiplicities; rho strictly between 0 and 1 gives positive inverse. Analytic Taylor remainder justifies sharp first-order local inverse but not global inversion. Independently assembled 40 real Jacobian matrices and compared full spectra.

Courtney gives recovery using mean plus Fourier moments THROUGH k, whereas zero moments THROUGH k-1 and a fixed-area tangent Jacobian on balanced k arcs constitute a narrower inverse-geometry question. The exact real two-level singular spectrum and k-independent condition number are not found in inspected primary results; the basic rigidity via Newton/self-inversive identities should not be overclaimed as independently deep.

final_claim: For k>=2 analytic consecutive Fourier modes and a measurable union of r nondegenerate separated arcs of normalized measure rho in (0,1), isometric restriction requires r>=k; at r=k all solutions are rotated equispaced equal arcs. On the fixed-area, rotation-quotiented endpoint tangent space the first k-1 Fourier moments have real squared singular values k(1 +/- |cos(pi rho)|)/(4pi^2), each k-1 times.
